config.title: Color Picker

intro.title: Color Picker
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an interactive color picker component that allows users to select colors using RGB sliders and displays the chosen color in real-time. You'll learn how to manage multiple pieces of related state using React's useState hook, where changes to red, green, and blue values automatically update the displayed color. The component will feature three range input sliders for RGB values and a color preview box that dynamically changes background color. You'll practice controlled components by connecting slider values to state variables, and learn how to convert RGB values into CSS color strings. This project demonstrates how React's state management enables building responsive, interactive user interfaces where multiple inputs work together to create a cohesive user experience.
intro.usecase: Color pickers are essential components in design tools like Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, and Canva, where users select colors for graphics, backgrounds, and text styling. They appear frequently in customization interfaces such as website theme builders, dashboard configuration panels, and e-commerce product customizers where users choose colors for items like clothing or accessories. Content management systems and blog editors use color pickers for text formatting and branding elements. Modern web applications also implement color pickers in user preference settings, allowing personalization of interface themes and accent colors.

objectives: Implement controlled input components for RGB color value manipulation
Apply state management techniques to synchronize color data across multiple UI elements
Construct dynamic styling that responds to real-time color input changes
Configure event handlers to capture and process user color selection interactions
Bind color picker inputs to update component state and trigger visual feedback
Render a functional color preview that displays the currently selected color values
Integrate multiple input controls to create a cohesive color selection interface

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Write the import statement at the top of your file to bring in React and the useState hook
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple items from a library
import { Component, Fragment } from 'react'
steps.expectedOutcome: React and useState are imported and ready to use in your color picker component
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: import React and useState from 'react' using the import statement. This will give you access to React components and state management.

steps.title: Create ColorPicker component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ColorPicker that returns JSX
steps.hint: Define a function that will serve as your main component. Make sure it returns some JSX content.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ColorPicker is defined and returns JSX
successCriteria: ColorPicker component is created and returns JSX content
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your ColorPicker component returns some JSX content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ColorPicker component needs to be defined as a function that returns JSX. Try creating a functional component.

steps.title: Initialize color state
steps.instruction: Inside your ColorPicker component, create a state variable called 'color' with an initial value of '#ff0000' using useState.
steps.hint: Use useState('#ff0000') and destructure it to get the color value and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating state for a counter
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a color state variable initialized to red (#ff0000) that can be used to track the currently selected color.
successCriteria: A state variable named 'color' is created with useState and initialized to '#ff0000'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using useState to create a state variable named 'color' with the initial value '#ff0000'.
steps.feedbackWrong: use useState('#ff0000') and destructure it into a color variable and its setter function.

steps.title: Define color change handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleColorChange that takes an event parameter and updates the color state with the event target's value.
steps.hint: Define the function inside your component, before the return statement. Use the color setter function from useState to update the state with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleColorChange function is defined that accepts an event parameter and updates the color state with the input value.
successCriteria: handleColorChange function is created that takes an event parameter and calls the color setter with event.target.value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your handleColorChange function takes an event parameter and uses the color setter function to update state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleColorChange function should take an event parameter and update the color state using event.target.value with your state setter function.

steps.title: Add main container div
steps.instruction: Replace the empty div in the return statement with a div that has className 'color-picker'
steps.hint: Use the className attribute to add the 'color-picker' CSS class to the div element
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: adding a CSS class to a div
steps.expectedOutcome: The return statement contains a div with className 'color-picker'
successCriteria: A div element with className 'color-picker' is returned from the component
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your div has the className attribute set to 'color-picker'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The div needs a className attribute with the value 'color-picker'. This will help style the color picker component.

steps.title: Add color input with change handler
steps.instruction: Add an input element inside the div with type='color', value set to the color state, and onChange wired to the handleColorChange function.
steps.hint: Use type='color' to create a color picker input, set the value attribute to your color state variable, and use onChange to call your handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: text input with value and onChange
<input type="text" value={name} onChange={handleNameChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: A color input element will be added inside the div, connected to the color state and change handler, creating a functional color picker.
successCriteria: An input element with type='color', value attribute set to color state, and onChange handler is added inside the div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your input has type='color', the value is set to your color state, and onChange calls your handler function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input needs three key attributes: type='color' for the color picker, value={color} to show the current color, and onChange={handleColorChange} to handle changes.

steps.title: Display selected color value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element that displays the current color state value
steps.hint:
Use JSX to add a

element that shows the color variable inside curly braces
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element appears that shows the current color value (e.g., #ff0000)
successCriteria: Paragraph element displays the color state value using JSX expression syntax
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the paragraph displays the color variable using curly braces in JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph should display the color state value. Use {color} inside the paragraph element to show the current color.

steps.title: Add color preview box
steps.instruction: Add a div element below the paragraph that displays the color value. Set its inline style with backgroundColor property to show the selected color.
steps.hint: Use the style attribute with an object containing backgroundColor set to the color state variable.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: div with inline background color
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element is added that shows a visual preview of the selected color by setting its background color to match the current color state.
successCriteria: A div element is added with inline style containing backgroundColor property set to the color state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the div has an inline style with backgroundColor set to the color state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The color preview div is missing. Add a div element with inline style backgroundColor set to the color state variable.

steps.title: Export ColorPicker component
steps.instruction: Add an export default statement at the bottom of the file to make the ColorPicker component available for use in other files.
steps.hint: Use 'export default ComponentName;' to export the component as the default export from this module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: exporting a component
export default MyButton;
steps.expectedOutcome: The ColorPicker component is exported as the default export, making it available for import and use in other files.
successCriteria: The file contains 'export default ColorPicker;' statement that exports the component
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using 'export default' followed by the component name 'ColorPicker'.
steps.feedbackWrong: add 'export default ColorPicker;' at the bottom of your file to make the component available for import in other files.

Centered content
